messages.author: 9207c07589137142
messages.subject: Error using nonparboot
parts:
Hi Ian, Andy, Marc, and Richard,

I'm having a problem generating confidence intervals for "projected"
in "colext". I'm largely following the process given in section 3 of
the colext vignette, except that I'm usuing real data, rather than
simulated data. I am able to fit sensible models and use the models
with "predict". "projected" gives me plausible expected values for the
occupancy state over time. When I go to bootstrap the SEs or
confidence intervals I get the following error message:

Error in data.frame(..., check.names = FALSE) :
arguments imply differing number of rows: 1520, 2344

Any ideas what's causing this? How to correct the problem?

The data are wildlife disease incidence data and there are lots of NAs
in the replicates. Or, perhaps it's due to transposition of the yearly
site covariates when building unmarkedMultFrame. I'm not clear on
using this transposition. Some unmarked documents seem to use it,
others don't.

Thanks,
Tom Ingersoll, post-doc
National Institute for Mathematical and Biological Synthesis

messages.author: 527e14923215b7e4
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Error using nonparboot
parts:
Hi Tom,

What version of unmarked are you using? Have you looked through the old questions about this on the list? This problem should be fixed in the most recent version on CRAN.

I'm not sure I understand your question about yearlySiteCovs. If you supply them as a list of matrices, then each matrix should have nSite rows and nYears columns.

Richard
